Why the China App Store listing still shows English

App Store Connect treats two settings as separate jobs:

  • Pricing and Availability → storefronts — which countries and regions can download your app. Checking China here makes the app available on the China App Store.
  • App Store tab → localizations — separate language rows (en-US, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, etc.) each with their own title, subtitle, keywords, description, screenshots, and release notes.

Enabling the China storefront does not auto-create Chinese copy. When a buyer on the China App Store opens your product page, Apple looks for a filled zh-Hans row. If that row is missing or empty, Apple falls back to en-US — or shows a mixed page (English text above Chinese screenshots, or vice versa). Neither reads as a finished listing to China buyers.

Common triggers we see from indie teams:

  • China checked under Pricing and Availability, but no Chinese (Simplified) localization was ever added
  • zh-Hans row exists but name, subtitle, or description were never saved — Connect shows the locale in the sidebar with blank fields
  • Metadata was drafted but the version with zh-Hans changes was never submitted for review
  • Screenshots are still the en-US set — even with Chinese text, English gallery art signals an unfinished localization

How to verify in App Store Connect

Walk through these checks before you assume Apple is “stuck” or caching wrong language:

Step 1 — Confirm China is available

App Store Connect → your app → Pricing and Availability → verify China appears under available storefronts. If China is off, no amount of zh-Hans copy will surface there.

Step 2 — Open the zh-Hans localization row

App Store Connect → your app → App Store tab → use the language dropdown (often top-left of the version editor). Look for Chinese (Simplified) or zh-Hans.

  • If zh-Hans is not in the list → click add localization and choose Simplified Chinese. You still need to fill fields.
  • If zh-Hans is listed but fields are empty or placeholder → the China storefront will fall back to en-US until you save Chinese text.

Step 3 — Inspect the four core text fields

With zh-Hans selected, confirm saved text in:

  • Name (title field)
  • Subtitle
  • Keywords (hidden from buyers, but part of the row)
  • Description

If any of these are blank, treat the localization as incomplete — not “done because the row exists.”

Step 4 — Check screenshots per localization

Screenshot sets are usually managed per localization. Open the zh-Hans screenshot slot for each required device size. If zh-Hans galleries are empty, Apple may show en-US art even when Chinese text fields are filled.

Step 5 — Confirm the version with zh-Hans was submitted

Metadata-only changes on live apps still go through App Review. If you filled zh-Hans locally but never submitted the version, the live China App Store page may still serve the last approved metadata — often English-only.

Step 6 — Spot-check on device

After approval, open your app’s product page on an iPhone signed into a China storefront account (or use Apple’s storefront preview tools). Compare what you see to the zh-Hans row in Connect — they should match. Mismatch usually means fallback or an unsubmitted version.

FAQ

Why does my China App Store listing still show English after I enabled China?

Enabling China under Pricing and Availability makes the app downloadable there — it does not create Chinese copy. Apple shows the zh-Hans localization row when it is filled; if zh-Hans title, subtitle, or description are empty, the product page falls back to en-US or shows a mixed English page.

How do I check whether zh-Hans is empty in App Store Connect?

Open your app in App Store Connect, go to the App Store tab, select the Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) localization from the language dropdown, and inspect whether name, subtitle, keywords, and description have saved text. An added row with blank fields means the China storefront still serves English fallback.

Does adding zh-Hans automatically translate my en-US listing?

No. Adding the localization row creates empty fields. You paste or type Chinese copy into each field independently. en-US and zh-Hans do not sync automatically.
